intro: Richmond upon Thames is one of the most desirable addresses in Greater London, and homeowners here tend to invest seriously in their properties. Wet room installations have become increasingly popular across the borough, not just as a practical upgrade but as a genuine way to add value and kerb appeal. Whether you're converting a tired en-suite or transforming a family bathroom, a well-executed wet room suits the lifestyle Richmond residents expect. The key is finding an installer who understands the specific demands of local housing stock — and there's more variety here than you might think.
localContext: Richmond upon Thames has a genuinely mixed property landscape that directly affects how a wet room installation unfolds. Edwardian semis — particularly common around Kew, East Sheen, and St Margarets — present real character but also challenges: timber suspended floors, older joinery, and bathroom dimensions that weren't designed with modern wet room drainage in mind. Post-war estates across Ham and Whitton tend to have solid concrete floors, which actually simplify tanking and drainage work considerably. Modern developments in Richmond town centre and along the riverside often have tighter floor-to-ceiling heights and pre-existing waterproofing that needs careful assessment before any strip-out begins. Richmond upon Thames also sits in a moderately hard water area, which is worth factoring into your material choices. Hard water accelerates limescale on glass screens and exposed fixtures, so specifying treated glass coatings and quality brass or chrome-plated fittings from the outset will save you a lot of maintenance effort over the years.
serviceDetail: A proper wet room installation in Richmond upon Thames is a multi-trade project, and understanding each stage helps you manage expectations and timelines. The process typically begins with a thorough site survey — a good installer will assess your floor structure, existing drainage position, soil pipe access, and load-bearing capacity before anything is agreed in writing. For Edwardian properties especially, this structural check is non-negotiable. Once the survey is complete and the design signed off, work begins with a full strip-out of the existing bathroom fittings, tiles, and floor coverings. If the floor is timber, a cement board substrate is usually installed to create a firm, waterproof base before tanking begins. Tanking — applying a continuous waterproof membrane across the floor and walls — is arguably the most critical stage. Rushing or skimping here is the single most common cause of wet room failures, and it should never be done in a single coat. Drainage channels are then set into the floor with a precise fall to avoid pooling, and your chosen wall and floor tiles are fitted. Tiling in a wet room requires more attention to grout joint sealing than a standard bathroom. Finally, sanitaryware, shower valves, screens or frameless glass panels, and all finishing trims are fitted and tested. From start to finish, most Richmond upon Thames wet room installations take between five and ten working days depending on complexity.
pricing: In Richmond upon Thames, you should budget realistically between £6,500 and £12,000 for a full wet room installation, with most mid-range projects landing around £8,000 to £9,500. Several factors push the cost toward the upper end: Edwardian floor structures requiring additional subfloor preparation, bespoke or large-format tiling, frameless glass screens, underfloor heating, and premium sanitaryware brands. Access constraints in older properties — narrow hallways, low loft access, restrictive parking for skips and deliveries — can also add to labour time. Straightforward conversions in post-war or modern homes with solid floors and existing soil pipe access tend to come in closer to the lower end of the range.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who works regularly in Richmond upon Thames makes a practical difference. They'll be familiar with the specific quirks of Edwardian building methods common to much of the borough, they'll have established relationships with local tile suppliers and bathroom showrooms, and they'll understand the permit and access requirements that come with working in residential streets across the area. A local installer also has a reputation to maintain on their doorstep, which concentrates the mind when it comes to workmanship and aftercare. For a project of this scale and cost, that local accountability really does matter.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in an Edwardian semi in Richmond upon Thames?
faqs.a: Yes, absolutely — but it requires more preparation than in a modern home. Timber suspended floors need a cement board overlay before tanking can begin, and the soil pipe position may need extending. A thorough pre-installation survey is essential. Many of the best wet rooms in the borough are in Edwardian properties, and with the right installer, the end result is excellent.

faqs.q: How do I protect a wet room from limescale given Richmond's hard water supply?
faqs.a: Richmond upon Thames has moderately hard water, so limescale on glass and chrome fittings is a genuine ongoing issue. Specify easy-clean glass treatments on any screens during installation, choose quality chrome or brushed brass fixtures, and squeegee the walls after each use. Some homeowners also install an inline water softener as part of the project, which significantly reduces long-term maintenance.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in Richmond upon Thames?
faqs.a: Most installations take between five and ten working days. A straightforward conversion in a post-war or modern property with good floor access is usually at the shorter end. Projects in older Edwardian homes requiring subfloor work, complex drainage repositioning, or bespoke tiling take longer. Your installer should give you a clear programme before work starts so you're not left without a working bathroom longer than necessary.

faqs.q: Does a wet room add value to a home in Richmond upon Thames?
faqs.a: In Richmond upon Thames's competitive property market, a well-designed wet room is generally seen as a premium feature that supports sale prices, particularly in family homes and properties targeting the executive rental market. The key is quality of finish — a poorly executed wet room can actually deter buyers, so specification and workmanship matter as much as the concept itself.
